lines.say: Incline or flat bench for your upper chest?
Your chest has an upper part, near your collarbone, and a bigger lower part.
Muscle activity studies show a moderate incline, about thirty degrees, shifts more of the work to the upper chest.
But go too steep, around forty five degrees or more, and your front shoulders take over.
Flat bench still trains your whole chest. Usually you can lift more weight on it, too.
So do both. Bench flat, and add incline at about thirty degrees.
And keep your shoulder blades pinched back on both.
